name: Audrey Hughes
life: “I still remember work shirts handed down from a cousin half my size.” On Wednesday, near the corner outside Coastal Barber, Audrey usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I kept taking the plain black ones for work shirts. Today I bought a whole packet to leave.
appearance: Audrey has close-cropped dark curls, a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, and a favorite piece of clothing, a dark green knitted vest. It usually goes with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. When somebody else has the floor, Audrey grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Audrey carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To replenish the common black buttons.
family: Sam Sharp is Audrey’s stepsibling. Audrey brings a spare shopping bag. Sam chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A boat for sale twice*, Sam says, “I used to polish that boat for a season pass.”
connections: Tali Moreno. Common work buttons let the card keep giving after the valuable ones go.
